text:
jamie: Heads-up — noticed streaming chat endpoints are allowing big bursts (lots of concurrent open streams) that spike downstream and trip our SLA fallback. Embeddings traffic is being throttled aggressively while streaming rides through. Can we align enforcement so streaming doesn't cannibalize token budgets?

rate-limiter-bot: ALERT: high burst detected for org-678 on /v1/stream. Applied soft-throttle (5s window) and notified eng-platform.

ravi: I saw that. My quick thought: make enforcement aware of endpoint semantics rather than a single token bucket. E.g. treat streaming as connection-limited, chat as low-latency token-rate, embeddings/rerank as high-throughput token-burst. Sketch:
```
policies:
  - name: streaming
    type: conn
    max_conn: 50
  - name: chat
    type: token
    rate: 2000/s
    burst: 8000
  - name: embeddings
    type: token
    rate: 10000/s
    burst: 20000
```
That lets us avoid a single global token bucket starving other endpoints.

marta: +1 on separate shapes, but we need a hierarchy: org-level commit -> per-endpoint overrides -> emergency cap. Otherwise customers with massive embed jobs still eat neighbor chat lanes. Also this matters for billing and alerts (we need to reflect which bucket charged).

ana: For the console UX: show per-route "headroom" and a visual indicator when traffic is being remapped to fallback. Add an action to toggle an "auto-fallback to smaller model" for embeddings when budget < X. For rollouts: policy changes must go through canary (5% of traffic) and autoscale the new bucket with a gradual ramp.

kevin: Be careful with complexity — more policy types means harder enforcement at the edge. We should add telemetry fields so we can answer why a request was limited: include `limit_reason`, `policy_id`, `endpoint_type` in traces and metrics. That will make postmortems and cost attribution simpler.

jamie: Agreed. Proposal for next steps: (1) spike: add connection-based limit for streaming on a probe cluster, (2) add `limit_reason` tag to traces + new console column, (3) wire up hierarchical quota evaluation (org->endpoint->key). Ravi/Marta — can you split the spike? I'll coordinate canary. @ravi @marta :thumbsup:

rate-limiter-bot: JOB CREATED: spike/ephemeral-policy-1855 assigned to ravi. ETA 2d.

jamie: Cool — if we can get basic telemetry in the spike we can iterate UX after 1st canary. Keeping this thread for tracking notes and quick q/a.
